findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State where the cluster docstrings live after extraction (move the substantive docstrings onto the extracted helpers and leave the BindingStore delegators as bare one-line pass-throughs) so the <700-LOC target and the unchanged-public-surface constraint can both hold.
evidence: Plan: 'the store keeps thin delegating methods, so no caller changes' — thin wrappers that keep their docstrings do not free the file's lines

binding_store.py at 787/800; get_baseline/set_baseline/get_peer_parent/set_peer_parent/seed_baselines_from_snapshot span lines 443-531 (~90 LOC) and are docstring-heavy (set_peer_parent's docstring alone is lines 497-507)

The <700 target requires shedding ~90 lines; if both the delegator (with docstring) and the helper (with docstring) carry the prose, the net reduction is far smaller and the new module inflates past intent
findings.finding: The plan's mechanism has an unresolved tension between 'thin delegating methods keep the public surface unchanged' and 'binding_store.py under 700 LOC': the extracted cluster's line count is dominated by large method docstrings, so if the delegating wrappers retain those docstrings the file will not shed the ~90 lines needed (787 -> <700). The plan does not state whether docstrings move to the extracted helpers (leaving delegators as bare one-liners) or stay on the delegators.
findings.location: Section 'What makes this non-trivial' + AC line 1 ('binding_store.py is under 700 LOC, and the new module is over 100')
scenarios: Implementer writes thin delegators that keep the existing docstrings; binding_store.py lands around 740-760 LOC and fails AC line 1 while the extraction is otherwise complete
Implementer duplicates docstrings across delegator and helper, inflating total LOC and defeating the headroom goal
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to 'What makes this non-trivial': the extracted module-level helpers carry the full docstrings; the retained BindingStore methods become one-line delegators (no docstring or a single-line reference), which is what actually sheds the ~90 lines while keeping every call site and test double valid.

Because the plan keeps BindingStore's public surface unchanged (thin delegates), none of these consumers require source edits; the defect is that the AC-promised 'grep-backed consumer list' is factually wrong, not that a build breaks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the peer-state consumer inventory from the symbol graph (find_referencing_symbols on get_baseline/set_baseline/get_peer_parent/set_peer_parent/seed_baselines_from_snapshot) AND a name-as-string grep for the getattr(binding_store, "...") forms, then correct AC line 4's list: add inbound_differ.py and adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py, and fix the inbound_fields attribution (it receives peer_parent as a parameter rather than calling get_peer_parent).
evidence: Plan prose: 'Its consumers are `outbound_field_diff`, `binding_walk` and now `inbound_fields` — none of which touch binding lifecycle.'

AC line 4: '`_BASELINE_FIELDS` moves WITH the cluster, and `outbound_field_diff` / `binding_walk` / `inbound_fields` still resolve their reads (a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket)' — the derivation method is stated as grep, whose known failure mode is silent omission.
inbound_differ.py:244: `_get_peer_parent = getattr(binding_store, "get_peer_parent", None)` — the real production caller of get_peer_parent, not listed.

adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:199-202: `get_peer_parent = getattr(binding_store, "get_peer_parent", None)` and :403 `arbitration_prev = binding_store.get_baseline(local_id)` — a production consumer of BOTH cluster methods, not listed.

inbound_fields.py diff_inbound_parent(...) signature takes `peer_parent: str | None = None` as a parameter — it does not call get_peer_parent, so naming 'inbound_fields' as the get_peer_parent consumer points at the wrong module.
findings.finding: The plan's consumer inventory for the extracted peer-state cluster ('Its consumers are outbound_field_diff, binding_walk and now inbound_fields') is self-described as grep-backed (AC line 4: 'a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket') rather than derived from the symbol reference graph, and is demonstrably inaccurate: it names inbound_fields as a get_peer_parent consumer when that module's diff_inbound_parent receives peer_parent as a parameter and never calls the method, while the two production call sites that DO invoke get_peer_parent — inbound_differ.py:244 and adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:199, both via getattr(binding_store, 'get_peer_parent', None) — are omitted, as is adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:403 which reads get_baseline. The getattr string form is precisely what an LSP structural lookup misses and a name-as-string grep must catch.
findings.location: 'The seam, which already exists' section ('Its consumers are outbound_field_diff, binding_walk and now inbound_fields') and AC line 4 ('a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket')
scenarios: inbound_differ.py:244 (getattr call site for get_peer_parent) — absent from the plan's consumer list; a future change that assumed the list was complete would miss the differ's dependence on the moved method.
adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:199/:403 (getattr call site for get_peer_parent and direct get_baseline read) — an entire production consumer file omitted from the inventory.
inbound_fields.py named as a get_peer_parent consumer when it only receives peer_parent as a parameter — the recorded inventory attributes the dependency to the wrong module.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'outbound_field_diff, binding_walk and now inbound_fields' with the graph-derived list: get_baseline is read by outbound_field_diff.py, binding_walk.py, adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py (and referenced in classify.py); get_peer_parent is called via getattr by inbound_differ.py and adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py, with inbound_fields.diff_inbound_parent consuming the peer_parent value passed in by inbound_differ. Note that all method call sites survive unchanged under the thin-delegator design; the list documents dependence, not patch sites.
